32720-what-we-saw-in-egypt.title: What We Saw In Egypt
32720-what-we-saw-in-egypt.creator: Unknown
32720-what-we-saw-in-egypt.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The welcome cry of "Suez! Suez!" resounded throughout the steamship _Bentinck_ one November morning. The passage up the Red Sea had been rough, and every one was glad to exchange the rolling and pitching of the vessel for land travelling.

74978-the-botanist-s-repository-for-new-.title: The Botanist S Repository For New And Rare Plants Vol 09 Of
74978-the-botanist-s-repository-for-new-.creator: Unknown
74978-the-botanist-s-repository-for-new-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Volkameria angustifolia is a dwarf branchy shrub flowering in great profusion about the middle of August. The blossoms are white and remarkably sweet-scented. It was communicated by Mr. Donn, Curator of the Cambridge Botanic garden, and is to be enumerated in the new edition of his Catalogue now in the press. It requires to be kept in the bark-bed in the hot-house, and is supposed to be a native of the Isle of France. We believe no other figure of it has been given.

arxiv-1910-09202.title: Conservation Laws in a Limit Order Book JR is a Fund Manager at Pine Tree and a Visiting Senior Research Fellow at King’s College London, jan.rosenzweig@kcl.ac.uk
arxiv-1910-09202.creator: Jan Rosenzweig
arxiv-1910-09202.description: Abstract We present a class of macroscopic models of the Limit Order Book to simulate the aggregate behaviour of market makers in response to trading flows. The resulting models are solved numerically and asymptotically, and a class of similarity solutions linked to order book formation and recovery is explored.

arxiv-2301-02228.title: MedKLIP: Medical Knowledge Enhanced Language-Image Pre-Training in Radiology
arxiv-2301-02228.creator: Chaoyi Wu, Xiaoman Zhang, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Weidi Xie
arxiv-2301-02228.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chaoyi Wu, Xiaoman Zhang, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Weidi Xie. In this paper, we consider enhancing medical visual-language pre-training (VLP) with domain-specific knowledge, by exploiting the paired image-text reports from the radiological daily practice.

arxiv-2505-01894.title: Certus: A domain specific language for confidence assessment in assurance cases
arxiv-2505-01894.creator: Simon Diemert, Jens H. Weber
arxiv-2505-01894.description: Abstract Assurance cases (ACs) are prepared to argue that a system has satisfied critical quality attributes. Many methods exist to assess confidence in ACs, including quantitative methods that represent confidence numerically. While quantitative methods are attractive in principle, existing methods suffer from issues related to interpretation, subjectivity, scalability, dialectic reasoning, and trustworthiness, which have limited their adoption.

arxiv-2505-20550.title: A detailed study on various phases in dissipative anisotropic Dicke model
arxiv-2505-20550.creator: Pragna Das, Saptarshi Saha
arxiv-2505-20550.description: Abstract We present a comprehensive study of different phases in the Dicke model incorporating both anisotropy and dissipation. We begin with a concise review of the quantum phase transition in this setting, highlighting how these two parameters shift the critical point.

britannica-1911-moran-edward.description: Article 'Moran, Edward' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. He emigrated with his family to America at the age of fifteen, and subsequently settled in Philadelphia, where after having followed his father’s trade of weaver, he became a pupil of James Hamilton and Paul Weber. In 1862 he became a pupil of the Royal Academy in London; he established a studio in New York in 1872, and for many years after 1877 lived in Paris.

pmc-10681359.title: Reconciling Paid Work and Informal Caregiving Among Older Adults: Implications for Work Interference With Family
pmc-10681359.creator: Shanika Yoshini Koreshi, Fiona Alpass
pmc-10681359.description: Background and ObjectivesMany older adults who combine paid work and informal caregiving responsibilities are often in work arrangements that differ from their preference. There is reason to believe that such work status incongruence may lead to work interference with family (WIF).

pmc-11422391.title: New insights in lipid metabolism: potential therapeutic targets for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11422391.creator: Yuan Cao, Lin-Wei Zhao, Zi-Xin Chen, Shao-Hua Li
pmc-11422391.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as being intertwined with the dysregulation of lipid metabolism. Lipids are a significant class of nutrients vital to all organisms, playing crucial roles in cellular structure, energy storage, and signaling. Alterations in the levels of various lipids in AD brains and dysregulation of lipid pathways and transportation have been implicated in AD pathogenesis.

pmc-11693065.title: ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT TO MEASURE SOCIAL CONNECTEDNESS IN OLDER ADULTS: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW
pmc-11693065.creator: JiYeon Choi, Seongmi Choi, Hun Kang, Jiyoung Shin
pmc-11693065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). While the importance of social connectedness in the lives of older adults is well-established, more comprehensive evidence is needed regarding its real-world operation. This study utilizes Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), increasingly employed in social and health sciences, to capture real-time social interactions in everyday environments, aiming to conduct an integrative review to understand multifactorial components of social connectedness and identify implementation strategies for older adults.

pmc-11713466.title: Derivation and Validation of the Cognitive Impairment Prediction Model in Older Adults: A National Cohort Study
pmc-11713466.creator: Mingyue Hu
pmc-11713466.description: BackgroundThis prediction model quantifies the risk of cognitive impairment. This aim of this study was to develop and validate a prediction model to calculate the 6‐year risk of cognitive impairment.MethodsParticipants from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS) 2008‐2014 and 2011‐2018 surveys were included for developing the cognitive impairment prediction model.

pmc-12652186.title: Medicinal Plants for a Healthy Gut Microbiome: Scientific Insights into Modern Herbal Applications
pmc-12652186.creator: Katarzyna Pacyga, Aleksandra Tabiś, Paweł Pacyga
pmc-12652186.description: The human gut microbiome is a complex ecosystem of microorganisms fundamental to human health, influencing metabolism, immunity, and neurological function. Dysbiosis, or an imbalance in this microbial community, is increasingly linked to a range of chronic diseases, from inflammatory bowel disease to metabolic syndrome.

pmc-12721150.title: Regulatory role of phosphatidylcholine metabolic reprogramming in colorectal cancer progression and neutrophil interactions
pmc-12721150.creator: Fu Cheng, Luji Huang, Yuanhong Peng, Lina Luo, Lin Zhong, Yongle Ju, Yan Lu, Manzhao Ouyang
pmc-12721150.description: SummaryColorectal cancer (CRC) remains a significant global health challenge due to its high incidence, mortality, and persistent issues with drug resistance, recurrence, and metastasis. Lipid metabolism reprogramming—a hallmark of CRC—plays a critical role in tumor progression. Mendelian randomization analysis established a causal relationship between phosphatidylcholine (PC) metabolism and CRC.

A randomized trial and an effectiveness study both found that anesthesiologists who used basic preventive measures (e.g.

pmc-13238240.title: A Rare Encounter: Documenting a Rotator Cuff Tear Associated With Idiopathic Rice Bodies
pmc-13238240.creator: Ekrem Özdemir, Oya Olcay Özdeş, Hüseyin Utku Özdeş, Shashank Kaushik
pmc-13238240.description: We share a case of a cuff tear caused by rice bodies, which typically occur in chronic inflammatory conditions and are often seen in autoimmune diseases. A 62‐year‐old patient presented with pain and restricted movement in the left shoulder. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed numerous rice body–like accumulations in the subacromial region, and a cuff tear was observed.

pmc-13275438.title: Perceived aging risk and private medical insurance intentions: education, subjective health, and a China–Malaysia comparison
pmc-13275438.creator: Zhangwei Zheng, Hafizuddin-Syah B.A.M, Hafizah Omar Zaki, Qin Lingda Tan
pmc-13275438.description: IntroductionPopulation aging raises uncertainty about future healthcare costs, pension adequacy, and financial security, yet evidence remains limited on how aging-related risk perceptions shape private medical insurance (PMI) intentions among adult consumers aged 18–64. This study examines whether perceived aging risk (AR) is associated with PMI purchase intentions and whether education, subjective health status, and national context condition this association.

pmc-13478138.title: Tissue factor and regenerative medicine: shaping cell and extracellular vesicle-based therapeutic approaches
pmc-13478138.creator: Van T. Hoang, Quyen Thi Nguyen, Duc Son Le, Lan Anh Thi Ngo, Liem Thanh Nguyen
pmc-13478138.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Regenerative medicine, characterized by breakthroughs in stem cell technology, cell-free therapies, and tissue engineering, holds immense promise for treating various diseases. However, along with the encouraging advancements in translational and clinical research, emerging evidence has demonstrated a potential risk of developing instant blood-mediated inflammatory reactions (IBMIRs) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) with the intravascular delivery of cellular products that do not naturally come into contact with blood.

pmc-13553664.title: Vascular geometry characterization for AI-based endovascular navigation
pmc-13553664.creator: Han-Ru Wu, Harry Robertshaw, Lisa Dwyer-Joyce, Thomas C Booth, Alejandro Granados
pmc-13553664.description: PurposeMechanical thrombectomy (MT) is a time-critical intervention for acute ischemic stroke; however, access remains limited due to a shortage of neuroradiologists and specialized centers. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers potential to automate endovascular navigation and improve accessibility, yet current models lack standardized frameworks to assess navigation difficulty for model training and evaluation.
